name: Maya
about: 16, in high school. Has done a few Scratch projects and one week of a Python course at school, then stopped. Curious, a bit unsure of herself.
app: A terminal app for splitting a restaurant bill between friends, with a tip, so nobody has to do the maths on their phone.
style: Short, plain sentences. Honest when she doesn't know something. Sometimes misses part of a question.

name: Dev
about: 34, backend developer, eight years of Java and Spring at a bank. Wants to try something other than Java on a side project.
app: A browser-based pub quiz: a host runs rounds from a laptop, teams answer on their phones, and a shared leaderboard updates live.
style: Precise and technical. Uses the right terms. Impatient with questions that feel like busywork, but answers properly.

name: Sam
about: 41, works in logistics. Hobbyist who has followed a couple of YouTube tutorials and copied code without fully understanding it.
app: A small desktop app that shows a grid of habits by day, so you can tick off what you did and see your streaks.
style: Terse, one-line answers, sometimes vague. Picks 'Not sure yet' on technical questions he doesn't follow.

name: Priya
about: 29, data analyst. Uses Python with pandas and Jupyter every day, but has never built an app that other people run.
app: A terminal tool that reads her bank's CSV exports, sorts spending into categories and prints a monthly summary with trends.
style: Organised and thorough. Writes in short paragraphs or bullet points. Thinks about edge cases in the data.

name: Leo
about: 14. Plays a lot of games and wants to make one. Has never written code, but has edited game config files.
app: A snake game in its own window, where the snake speeds up as it eats and the high score is saved.
style: Enthusiastic, informal, sometimes off-topic. Lots of ideas, few details. Gets the order of things wrong.

name: Ana
about: 26, just finished a web development bootcamp (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, a little React). Job hunting and wants a portfolio project.
app: A website where people post recipes, save other people's, and search by the ingredients they have at home.
style: Clear and motivated. Mentions what employers want. Sometimes over-scopes and lists too many features.

name: Tomás
about: 20, second-year college student. His course requires C# for this project. Comfortable with loops and classes, not much else.
app: A desktop inventory app for his part-time job at a bike shop: add parts, track how many are left, and flag what to reorder.
style: Practical and direct. Mentions the course requirements. Already knows the language is decided.
